Summary

LlamaRisk recommends the following parameter changes based on user behavior, on-chain liquidity, and position health observed in the latest review of Aave V3 reserves.

Aave V3 Core:

  • Increase supply cap for BTC.b from 20 to 40.

Aave V3 Mantle:

  • Increase supply cap for USDe from 10,000,000 to 20,000,000.
  • Increase borrow cap for USDe from 9,000,000 to 18,000,000.

Aave V3 Base:

  • Increase supply cap for cbETH from 50,000 to 75,000.

Aave V3 Monad:

  • Increase supply cap for USDe from 20,000,000 to 40,000,000.
  • Increase borrow cap for USDe from 18,000,000 to 36,000,000.
  • Increase supply cap for sUSDe from 20,000,000 to 40,000,000.
  • Reduce supply cap for mUSD from 100,000,000 to 50,000,000.
  • Reduce borrow cap for mUSD from 50,000,000 to 25,000,000.

BTC.b (Aave V3 Core)

BTC.b has reached 99.7% supply cap utilization (19 / 20) on the Aave V3 Core instance. The reserve is configured as collateral only.

Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, July 30, 2026

The top BTC.b suppliers run health factors between 1.14 and 2.10 with a median of 1.52, and eight of the nine carry outstanding debt. Debt is denominated entirely in stablecoins, across USDe, GHO, USDT, and USDC, so the cohort holds stablecoin borrowings against BTC.b collateral whose health factor stability tracks the BTC price.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the supply cap from 20 to 40 on Aave V3 Core. The reserve sits at 99.7% cap utilization and the proposed cap lands at approximately 49.9% post-change utilization.

USDe (Aave V3 Mantle)

USDe has reached 99.8% supply cap utilization (9,982,168 / 10,000,000) and 17.0% borrow cap utilization (1,532,090 / 9,000,000) on the Aave V3 Mantle instance.

Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, July 30, 2026

Two of the top five USDe suppliers carry outstanding debt at health factors between 1.03 and 1.05, and the remainder hold the asset without offsetting borrowings. That debt is denominated in USDT0, GHO, and USDC, and USDe is usable as collateral only within the stablecoin E-Mode categories, where the tight health factor cluster reflects the high liquidation thresholds applied to correlated stablecoin pairs.

Borrow Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, July 30, 2026

The top USDe borrowers run health factors between 1.27 and 3.81 with a median of 1.92, and all carry outstanding debt. Borrowing is drawn against WETH and FBTC collateral, so health factor stability in this cohort tracks the ETH and BTC price.

Recommendation

We recommend raising the supply cap from 10,000,000 to 20,000,000 and raising the borrow cap from 9,000,000 to 18,000,000 on Aave V3 Mantle. The supply side sits at 99.8% cap utilization and lands at approximately 49.9% post-change utilization, while the borrow side moves from 17.0% to approximately 8.5%.

cbETH (Aave V3 Base)

cbETH is currently at 89.0% supply cap utilization (44,524 / 50,000) on the Aave V3 Base instance. The reserve is configured as collateral only.

Supply Distribution


Source: LlamaRisk, July 30, 2026

All twenty of the top cbETH suppliers carry outstanding debt, with health factors between 1.02 and 12.71 and a median of 1.14. WETH is the dominant borrowed asset by a wide margin, with USDC second, and cbETH is eligible in both the ETH-correlated and the cbETH/WETH E-Mode categories, so health factor stability in the cohort tracks the cbETH versus ETH spread.

Recommendation

governance_posts.description:
Summary

LlamaRisk proposes deprecating Chainlink price feeds for a set of long-tail assets deployed across Aave V2 or V3 reserves, feeds that Chainlink itself has classified as high or very high operational risk as the underlying assets have lost meaningful adoption and liquidity, leaving too little trading activity to price them reliably. The set spans 10 deployments, part of which are already deprecated, with aggregate affected supply of $6.76M and aggregate debt of $4.29M.

Previously applied as part of Aave V2 Continued Deprecation Steps, this round of changes expands to some of the Aave V3 deployments, as these assets have already been deprecated for an extended period of time and continue to experience a decline in adoption, which in turn affects the stability of the secondary market price feeds employed by Chainlink. Deprecating troubled or inactive reserves is a standard, well-established part of Aave governance. The same process has been applied to other assets before, including the full deprecation of DPI across Aave deployments and the TUSD offboarding plan, and this proposal follows the same playbook.

Motivation

The reserves in scope share a common deprecation reason: each underlying asset has either lost meaningful adoption or held its peg only intermittently over a sustained period, and in several cases both. As activity migrated away, secondary market liquidity thinned to the point where the asset’s market price is no longer a dependable input for valuing collateral and debt on a lending protocol. Pricing a thinly traded or persistently depegged asset from its live market feed is inherently fragile, because the reported value can drift well away from any defensible fair value and can be moved by a small amount of trading volume.

For this reason Chainlink has classified the price feeds behind these reserves as high or very high risk meaning that they should no longer be used to price assets on Aave. Continuing to mark positions against a feed whose underlying market has deteriorated leaves the protocol exposed to stale or manipulable valuations, which on a lending market translate directly into mispriced collateral, unfair liquidations, or debt that is no longer fully backed.

These reserves nonetheless still carry live positions on Aave, held as collateral, as debt, or both, so the feeds cannot simply be switched off. Each reserve instead requires an individual remedy: the live oracle is replaced with a fixed-price adapter and paired with a controlled set of parameter changes so the remaining positions can be wound down in an orderly fashion. The approach is tailored on a per-asset basis, where the non-frozen assets are also frozen as part of the oracle deprecation.

Aave V3 Reserves & Markets

Twenty-one V3 reserves fall under this round of oracle deprecation. Six carry material exposure and are analysed individually below: LUSD and FRAX on both Ethereum Core and Arbitrum, RPL on Ethereum Core, and USDm on Celo. Together they hold $3.50M of supply and $1.47M of debt, and only $13.0K of the supplied balance is enabled as collateral, so the exposure sits almost entirely on the supply and debt sides rather than in collateral risk. The remaining 15 V3 reserves, spread across Arbitrum, Avalanche, Ethereum, Optimism, Polygon, Scroll and the EtherFi instance, hold a further $231.2K of supply and $48.2K of debt and are handled with the simplified treatment described in the Negligible Exposure Reserves section.

LUSD on Aave V3 Ethereum Core

LUSD is the decentralised, ETH-backed stablecoin issued by the Liquity protocol. On Aave V3 Ethereum Core it carries $2.01M of supply across 127 wallets and $664.7K of debt across 60 wallets. Of that supply, only $12.2K across 15 wallets is enabled as collateral at the current 77% LT.

The active feed is a Chainlink LUSD/USD secondary market price feed used in a stable price cap adapter with a $1.10 price cap, currently reporting a price of $1.00. Hardcoding the oracle to a fixed value removes the price manipulation vector for both the LUSD collateral and LUSD debt without materially repricing the position relative to its current accounting value.

Source: LlamaRisk, July 28th, 2026

Position breakdown

  • Supplied only (not borrowed against): 123 wallets, $1.98M of LUSD, including 11 that have LUSD enabled as collateral but carry no debt.
  • Used as collateral backing debt: 4 wallets, $7.4K of LUSD, backing only $160 of borrowing.
  • Borrowed: 60 wallets, $664.6K of LUSD debt.

Borrower health

Across the 63 wallets that borrow LUSD or post it as collateral, the median HF is 1.81 and the 10th percentile is 1.03. 6 are already below HF 1, 2 more sit in the [1.0, 1.05] band where a 1% adverse move would tip them into liquidation, and 26 sit above HF 2.

Source: LlamaRisk, July 28th, 2026

Co-position patterns

The top 10 LUSD borrowers post $11.40M of collateral between them, almost entirely WETH at $8.02M and WBTC at $3.18M, with a small LINK remainder. LUSD is being borrowed against blue-chip collateral, not held as a directional position.

Source: LlamaRisk, July 28th, 2026

Recommendation

The reserve is frozen and its supply and borrow caps are reduced to one. The oracle is hardcoded at $1.00. Because slope2 only affects the borrow rate once utilization rises above the optimal point, raising it alone would leave the current 2.1% borrow APR at 33% utilization unchanged. The RF is therefore raised from 20% to 99%, redirecting almost all interest income from suppliers to the treasury. With their yield gone, suppliers are expected to withdraw, which lifts utilization and with it the borrow rate. The IRM base rate is also raised to 5%, a moderate but immediate repayment incentive that applies at every utilization level, and slope2 to 100% so that once utilization does cross the optimal point the borrow rate climbs steeply. As this is the first step of the deprecation, sharper rate increases are deliberately left for a later round.

Aggregate IRM and RF Recommendation

IRM and RF changes are evaluated reserve by reserve against three conditions: current utilization, the current borrow rate, and the health of the outstanding debt. Where utilization already sits near 100% and the borrow rate is significant, no change is needed, because the existing configuration already makes the residual debt expensive to hold. Where utilization is low, raising slope2 alone would change nothing, because slope2 only enters the borrow rate once utilization rises above the optimal point.

For those reserves the first change is to the RF: raising it to 99% redirects almost all interest income from suppliers to the treasury, and with their yield gone suppliers are expected to withdraw, which lifts utilization and with it the borrow rate. The IRM base rate is raised to 5% alongside, giving borrowers a steady repayment incentive at any utilization without forcing immediate liquidations, and slope2 to 100% so that once utilization does cross the optimal point the borrow rate climbs steeply. Sharper increases are deliberately deferred to a later round of the deprecation.

Finally, where the outstanding debt sits predominantly with wallets already below HF 1, or cannot be repaid at all, rate increases are avoided altogether, because interest accrual on unrecoverable positions only inflates the bad debt the protocol will eventually write off. Across this set that applies to AMPL on Aave V2 and to the transfer-frozen sUSD reserves on Aave V2 Ethereum and Aave V3 Optimism, all of which have their IRM flattened to zero.

Stressed-Dominant Reserves

AMPL on Aave V2 Ethereum holds $2.60M of outstanding debt of which $2.60M (100.0%) sits with borrowers whose protocol-reported HF is below one. sUSD on Aave V2 Ethereum is a second effectively-stressed case: its debt is shown as predominantly healthy by reported HF, but with transfers frozen the full $13.3K is unrecoverable. Rate escalation is deliberately avoided here: at 99% utilization the current IRM already accrues at roughly 317% APR onto debt that will not be repaid, so every block compounds the eventual write-off. The IRM is instead flattened to base 0%, slope1 0%, and slope2 0%, freezing the unrecoverable debt at its current level while the fixed oracle caps its accounting value.

Treasury Holdings

The Aave treasury Collector, largely through accumulated RF income, is itself a major supplier of several reserves in scope. It holds 100% of the USDP supply ($200.5K, of which $151.0K is withdrawable at current liquidity), 98% of AMPL ($1.62M, effectively none withdrawable at 99% utilization), 40% of TUSD ($115.3K, all withdrawable), 67% of sUSD ($45.8K, not withdrawable while transfers are frozen), 73% of MAI on Avalanche ($15.0K) and 87% of miMATIC on Polygon ($7.8K). Withdrawing the withdrawable balances as part of the wind-down recovers value for the DAO and drains the affected reserves faster. The same housekeeping applies to legacy treasury positions outside this scope, such as GUSD on Aave V2 Ethereum.

Negligible Exposure Reserves

The reserves below each carry less than $50K of combined supply and debt. They were analysed with the same methodology as the material reserves above, but given the small exposure the full per-asset figures are omitted for conciseness and consolidated into the table below. The remedy is the same: the oracle is replaced with a fixed-price adapter, which freezes each position’s accounting value and removes the manipulation surface of the thinly traded feed. Stablecoins still trading within 3% of their dollar peg (LUSD, FRAX and MAI/miMATIC) are hardcoded at $1.00, matching the treatment of the material stablecoin reserves. Significantly depegged stablecoins are instead fixed at their current price, so the switch to the fixed adapter reprices nothing: sUSD on Optimism, trading far below its peg and non-transferable under SIP-423, is set at its live reported value of $0.2763. With the token frozen, the reserve, where the treasury Collector holds 56% of the supply, can no longer be exited and the fixed price simply freezes its accounting. For the same reason its IRM is flattened to zero rather than moved to the standard base 20% and slope2 40%: accrual on non-repayable debt only inflates the eventual write-off. The volatile assets are fixed at the trailing 6 month average of the existing feed with no premium or discount. The IRM is set to a 20% base rate with slope2 reduced to 40%, so every residual borrow position pays a meaningful rate even at low utilization, encouraging repayment, while the flattened slope2 prevents runaway interest accrual on positions that are never closed. The same treatment was previously applied when sunsetting the DPI reserve on Aave V2.

Summary

LlamaRisk proposes deprecating Chainlink price feeds for a set of long-tail assets deployed across Aave V2 or V3 reserves, feeds that Chainlink itself has classified as high or very high operational risk as the underlying assets have lost meaningful adoption and liquidity, leaving too little trading activity to price them reliably. The set spans 10 deployments, part of which are already deprecated, with aggregate affected supply of $6.76M and aggregate debt of $4.29M.

Previously applied as part of Aave V2 Continued Deprecation Steps, this round of changes expands to some of the Aave V3 deployments, as these assets have already been deprecated for an extended period of time and continue to experience a decline in adoption, which in turn affects the stability of the secondary market price feeds employed by Chainlink. Deprecating troubled or inactive reserves is a standard, well-established part of Aave governance. The same process has been applied to other assets before, including the full deprecation of DPI across Aave deployments and the TUSD offboarding plan, and this proposal follows the same playbook.

Motivation

The reserves in scope share a common deprecation reason: each underlying asset has either lost meaningful adoption or held its peg only intermittently over a sustained period, and in several cases both. As activity migrated away, secondary market liquidity thinned to the point where the asset’s market price is no longer a dependable input for valuing collateral and debt on a lending protocol. Pricing a thinly traded or persistently depegged asset from its live market feed is inherently fragile, because the reported value can drift well away from any defensible fair value and can be moved by a small amount of trading volume.

For this reason Chainlink has classified the price feeds behind these reserves as high or very high risk meaning that they should no longer be used to price assets on Aave. Continuing to mark positions against a feed whose underlying market has deteriorated leaves the protocol exposed to stale or manipulable valuations, which on a lending market translate directly into mispriced collateral, unfair liquidations, or debt that is no longer fully backed.

These reserves nonetheless still carry live positions on Aave, held as collateral, as debt, or both, so the feeds cannot simply be switched off. Each reserve instead requires an individual remedy: the live oracle is replaced with a fixed-price adapter and paired with a controlled set of parameter changes so the remaining positions can be wound down in an orderly fashion. The approach is tailored on a per-asset basis, where the non-frozen assets are also frozen as part of the oracle deprecation.

Aave V3 Reserves & Markets

Twenty-one V3 reserves fall under this round of oracle deprecation. Six carry material exposure and are analysed individually below: LUSD and FRAX on both Ethereum Core and Arbitrum, RPL on Ethereum Core, and USDm on Celo. Together they hold $3.50M of supply and $1.47M of debt, and only $13.0K of the supplied balance is enabled as collateral, so the exposure sits almost entirely on the supply and debt sides rather than in collateral risk. The remaining 15 V3 reserves, spread across Arbitrum, Avalanche, Ethereum, Optimism, Polygon, Scroll and the EtherFi instance, hold a further $231.2K of supply and $48.2K of debt and are handled with the simplified treatment described in the Negligible Exposure Reserves section.

The active feed is a Chainlink LUSD/USD secondary market price feed used in a stable price cap adapter with a $1.10 price cap, currently reporting a price of $1.00. Hardcoding the oracle to a fixed value removes the price manipulation vector for both the LUSD collateral and LUSD debt without materially repricing the position relative to its current accounting value.

Source: LlamaRisk, July 28th, 2026

Recommendation

The reserve is frozen and its supply and borrow caps are reduced to one. The oracle is hardcoded at $1.00. Aggregate IRM and RF Recommendation

IRM and RF changes are evaluated reserve by reserve against three conditions: current utilization, the current borrow rate, and the health of the outstanding debt. Where utilization already sits near 100% and the borrow rate is significant, no change is needed, because the existing configuration already makes the residual debt expensive to hold. Where utilization is low, raising slope2 alone would change nothing, because slope2 only enters the borrow rate once utilization rises above the optimal point.

For those reserves the first change is to the RF: raising it to 99% redirects almost all interest income from suppliers to the treasury, and with their yield gone suppliers are expected to withdraw, which lifts utilization and with it the borrow rate. The IRM base rate is raised to 5% alongside, giving borrowers a steady repayment incentive at any utilization without forcing immediate liquidations, and slope2 to 100% so that once utilization does cross the optimal point the borrow rate climbs steeply. Sharper increases are deliberately deferred to a later round of the deprecation.

Finally, where the outstanding debt sits predominantly with wallets already below HF 1, or cannot be repaid at all, rate increases are avoided altogether, because interest accrual on unrecoverable positions only inflates the bad debt the protocol will eventually write off. Across this set that applies to AMPL on Aave V2 and to the transfer-frozen sUSD reserves on Aave V2 Ethereum and Aave V3 Optimism, all of which have their IRM flattened to zero.

Hi dear aave community :)

I’d like to share Aave DeFi Watcher, a browser extension I built to make monitoring Aave positions simple, fast, and privacy-friendly.

I originally started building it because the previously shared Aave Monitor extension appears to no longer function reliably. For example, many addresses currently return “Failed to fetch” instead of account data. It also only supports Aave V3, while I wanted a tool that could monitor positions across Aave V2, V3, and V4. Since I needed a working solution myself, I decided to build one from scratch.

Features

  • Total Collateral
  • Total Debt
  • Available to Borrow
  • Loan-to-Value (LTV)
  • Liquidation Threshold
  • Health Factor
  • Monitor multiple wallet addresses
  • Support for Aave V2, V3, and V4
  • Support for multiple networks including Ethereum, Arbitrum, Optimism, Base, Polygon, and Avalanche
  • Desktop notifications for Health Factor alerts
  • Privacy Mode to hide balances while continuing to monitor your positions
  • Automatic RPC fallback for improved reliability

One of my favorite features is the extension badge, which displays the Health Factor of your selected address directly on the browser toolbar, allowing you to monitor your position at a glance.

The extension is completely read-only. It never asks you to connect a wallet or sign transactions. All account data is fetched directly from Aave’s public smart contracts.

Chrome Web Store

chromewebstore.google.com

Aave DeFi Watcher - Chrome Web Store

Monitor your Aave health factor and liquidation risk in real time across chains.

I built this extension for my own daily use and decided to share it with the community. It’s actively maintained, and I plan to continue adding new features and supporting future Aave releases.

I’d really appreciate any feedback, bug reports or feature suggestions from the community :))

governance_posts.title: Introducing Maxshot AI as a Strategy Operator in the Aave Ecosystem
governance_posts.description:
1. Summary

This proposal introduces Maxshot AI to the Aave community as a complementary, value-accretive yield optimization and distribution layer.

As Maxshot is already integrated with Aave V3 markets across multiple chains, this proposal does not request any protocol parameter changes, risk parameter updates, or direct integrations. Instead, it seeks community awareness, feedback, and formal ecosystem recognition of Maxshot as a third-party strategy operator that enhances capital efficiency and user experience for Aave.

By leveraging AI-driven, non-discretionary agents, Maxshot simplifies access to optimized, omni-chain yield opportunities, with the goal of increasing total value locked (TVL), capital efficiency, and liquidity stickiness across Aave markets.

2. Abstract

Maxshot AI operates as an intelligent yield optimization layer built on top of Aave and other DeFi protocols. It automatically routes and rebalances capital across chains and markets using deterministic, AI-driven agents to maximize risk-adjusted returns.

This proposal aims to align the Aave community with an existing ecosystem partner that already contributes capital flows into Aave liquidity pools and improves user access to yield opportunities without introducing additional protocol risk.

3. Motivation

Aave is a foundational DeFi liquidity protocol with robust risk management, transparent governance, and deployments across multiple networks. While its multi-chain expansion is a core strength, it also introduces structural inefficiencies that create opportunities for complementary, user-layer optimization.

Key Challenges

  • Liquidity Fragmentation: Liquidity is distributed across multiple Aave deployments, requiring users to manually bridge assets, compare rates, and manage positions across chains.

  • Operational Complexity: Actively managing positions across multiple markets and networks is time-intensive and costly, leading to suboptimal capital allocation.

  • Uneven Utilization: Friction at the user layer can result in idle liquidity and inconsistent utilization across Aave markets.

Maxshot’s Role

Maxshot AI acts as a non-custodial, intelligent routing and optimization layer on top of Aave, improving capital efficiency and user experience through automated, rules-based yield optimization—without modifying or competing with Aave’s core protocol.

4. Specification: Maxshot Overview

Maxshot AI is an AI Agent Factory, an AI-native, automation-first infrastructure layer designed to build, deploy, and coordinate autonomous agents for on-chain capital optimization.

At its core, Maxshot provides a standardized framework for creating protocol-aware, risk-constrained AI agents that can observe market conditions, reason over strategy sets, and execute actions across DeFi systems. These agents operate continuously within predefined risk models and governance-aligned parameters, enabling scalable and transparent automation at the infrastructure level.

Key Characteristics

  • Deterministic, Continuous Execution

    Agents operate autonomously and continuously, responding to market changes without manual intervention. All decisions follow transparent, rules-based logic that is auditable and verifiable on-chain, eliminating discretionary risk.

  • Full On-Chain Transparency

    Every allocation, rebalance, and performance metric is recorded on-chain and available for real-time community review, enabling ongoing verification of compliance and protocol impact.

  • Separation of Concerns

    Maxshot enforces a strict separation between optimization logic (Strategy Layer), safety constraints (Risk Layer), and on-chain interactions (Execution Layer). This design ensures that strategy decisions cannot bypass risk controls and that all actions remain auditable.

The first flagship product built on this framework is Maxshot Omni Yield Aggregator, an omni-chain, multi-protocol yield optimization system live across multiple blockchains. Powered by a coordinated network of autonomous agents, the aggregator dynamically allocates capital in real time rather than relying on static strategies or manual rebalancing.

As the agent factory expands, Maxshot is designed to support new on-chain use cases beyond yield optimization, while maintaining strict alignment with protocol risk frameworks and ecosystem incentives.

5. Technical Architecture

Maxshot follows a protocol-agnostic, modular architecture optimized for transparency, security, and auditability. The system consists of three distinct layers:

Strategy Layer

Defines optimization logic and allocation objectives by analyzing real-time market data across Aave and other protocols. It generates allocation recommendations but has no execution authority.

Risk Layer

Acts as the system’s safety guardrail, enforcing predefined constraints such as protocol, asset, and chain exposure limits. Any action that violates these rules is automatically blocked and logged for transparency.

Execution Layer

Handles all on-chain operations, including deposits, withdrawals, and rebalancing. Execution is deterministic and fully auditable, and only proceeds after Risk Layer approval.

This three-layer architecture ensures that strategy optimization, risk management, and execution transparency are never compromised. Each layer operates independently, and no single layer has authority over the entire system. This design reduces the risk of catastrophic failures and ensures that the Aave community retains full visibility and control over Maxshot’s operations.

6. Rationale & Differentiation

Maxshot AI is an AI-native, automation-native financial infrastructure designed to manage and optimize on-chain financial activities.

Unlike traditional yield aggregators that rely on static strategies or manual rebalancing, Maxshot operates as a network of non-discretionary, autonomous agents that continuously evaluate market conditions and execute allocation decisions in real time, strictly within predefined risk constraints and governance-aligned parameters.

Core Advantages

  1. Omni-chain, Multi-protocol Optimization

    Capital is optimized globally across chains and protocols rather than siloed within a single deployment.

  2. Agent-driven (Non-discretionary) Execution

    Deterministic agents execute strategies continuously without human intervention or discretionary decision-making.

  3. Separation of Strategy, Risk, and Execution

    A modular architecture enforces clear boundaries between optimization logic, risk controls, and execution, enhancing security, transparency, and independent auditability.

This architecture allows Maxshot to function not merely as a yield aggregator, but as a general-purpose AI agent platform, where additional agents (such as risk agents, liquidity routing agents, governance-aware execution agents, and protocol-specific strategy agents) can be composed and deployed over time.

7. Live Deployments & Metrics

Maxshot has been live in production since December 2025, and has already attracted meaningful TVL, demonstrating operational readiness and early market validation.

The platform currently manages approximately $9.8M in total TVL across live deployments, including ~$1.8M in the Omni USDC vault. All deployments are fully on-chain and publicly verifiable, reducing the governance and execution risk typically associated with new strategy operators.

  • Technical Capability

Maxshot is built on proven DeFi architecture and continuous monitoring systems, and employs industry-standard security practices including multi-signature controls, timelocks, emergency and pause mechanisms.

  • Operational Duration

Maxshot has been live in production for over one month, providing sufficient operational history to demonstrate system stability, performance consistency, and effective risk management.

10. User & Ecosystem Benefits

For Users

  • One-click access to optimized, omni-chain yield

    Users deposit into a single vault and gain exposure to the best available risk-adjusted yields across supported markets and supported chains, without manually bridging or managing multiple positions.

  • Automated capital rebalancing with reduced operational overhead

    Autonomous agents continuously monitor market conditions and rebalance capital in real time, saving users time, gas costs, and the need for active position management.

  • Transparent, real-time performance visibility

    All allocations, rebalances, and returns are recorded on-chain, allowing users to independently verify performance, fees, and capital deployment at any time.

For DAOs & Institutions

  • Custom or branded strategies with tailored risk profiles

    DAOs and institutions can launch protocol- or treasury-specific strategies with defined risk parameters, allocation constraints, and optimization objectives aligned with their mandates.

  • Treasury-grade reporting and on-chain transparency

    Detailed analytics, allocation breakdowns, and historical transaction records support institutional treasury management, auditability, and compliance requirements.

For the Aave Protocol

  • Increased TVL and user growth

    Lower access friction and automated yield optimization attract new users and capital into Aave markets across multiple networks.

  • Improved capital efficiency across markets

    Dynamic allocation routes liquidity to the most productive pools, reducing idle capital and improving overall utilization rates.

  • Enhanced liquidity stickiness

    Consistent, optimized returns encourage users to retain capital within the ecosystem rather than migrating to competing protocols.

This proposal requests the following from the Aave community:

  • Community review and feedback on Maxshot’s proposed role, design, and alignment within the Aave ecosystem, including any concerns or recommendations from contributors and risk stakeholders.

  • Recognition of Maxshot AI as a complementary, third-party strategy operator, operating on top of Aave without modifying core protocol parameters or competing with native Aave products.

  • Exploration of optional future collaboration opportunities, such as co-marketing initiatives, ecosystem showcases, or joint educational efforts, subject to community interest and further discussion.

11. Formal Requests

Maxshot requests the following from the Aave community:

  • Community review and feedback on Maxshot’s proposed role, design, and alignment within the Aave ecosystem, including any concerns or recommendations from contributors and risk stakeholders.

  • Recognition of Maxshot AI as a complementary, third-party strategy operator, operating on top of Aave without modifying core protocol parameters or competing with native Aave products.

  • Exploration of optional future collaboration opportunities, such as co-marketing initiatives, ecosystem showcases, or joint educational efforts, subject to community interest and further discussion.

12. Risk Assessment

This proposal introduces no direct protocol risk, as:

  • No changes to Aave smart contracts or protocol parameters are requested or required

  • Aave governance retains full control over all protocol operations, risk settings, and upgrade decisions

  • Maxshot interacts with Aave solely as a standard external user, using existing, permissionless interfaces

Any risks specific to Maxshot are isolated from the Aave protocol and are mitigated through a modular system architecture, deterministic and transparent on-chain execution, continuous monitoring and automated safeguards, and the operational experience of the Maxshot team managing live, multi-chain deployments.

13. Community Discussion Topics

We welcome feedback from the Aave community on the following points:

  • The role of AI-driven yield optimizers within the Aave ecosystem, including how automated strategy layers can complement Aave’s core markets while respecting protocol risk frameworks.

  • Desired benchmarks, safeguards, or constraints for recognized strategy operators, such as transparency standards, risk limits, reporting expectations, or operational maturity.

  • Best practices for collaboration between Aave and ecosystem partners, including governance communication, risk disclosures, and ongoing monitoring.

  • Preferences for future integrations or co-branded initiatives, such as ecosystem showcases, educational content, or user-facing integrations that align with Aave’s long-term strategy.

14. Next Steps

Following a community feedback period, the goal is to reach consensus on recognizing Maxshot as an official ecosystem partner. Maxshot remains committed to transparent engagement and ongoing communication with the Aave DAO.

15. Resources & Contacts

For questions, feedback, or collaboration inquiries, please reach out through the following channels:

  • X: https://twitter.com/MaxshotAI
